title: Chapter 7 Quiz: Authentication & Authorization
description: Test your knowledge of Django’s authentication system, permissions, and customization.

questions.question: Which Django model stores user accounts?
questions.explanation: The `User` model in `django.contrib.auth.models` is the default user model.

questions.question: Passwords in Django are stored in plain text in the database.
questions.explanation: False. Django hashes passwords using strong algorithms (PBKDF2 by default).

questions.question: Which method should you use to create a new user with a hashed password?
questions.explanation: `create_user()` automatically hashes the password and creates the user.

questions.question: To check a user’s password, you call `user.______(password)`.
questions.explanation: `check_password` compares the plain text password with the stored hash.

questions.question: Which decorator ensures that a view is only accessible to logged‑in users?
questions.explanation: `@login_required` is the standard decorator.

questions.question: The `is_staff` flag gives a user all permissions.
questions.explanation: False. `is_staff` only allows access to the admin site; `is_superuser` gives all permissions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `authenticate()` function?
options: It verifies credentials and returns a user object
questions.explanation: `authenticate()` validates credentials and returns the user object if valid, otherwise None.

questions.question: The URL pattern for the built‑in login view, when including `'accounts/'`, is `accounts/______/`.
questions.explanation: The login view is at `/accounts/login/` by default.

questions.question: How do you check if a user has the permission to delete a Post?
questions.explanation: Permissions are in the format `app_label.permission_codename`.

questions.question: Django automatically creates add, change, and delete permissions for every model.
questions.explanation: True. These are created when you run migrations for the first time.

questions.question: What is the best way to add extra fields (e.g., bio, location) to the User model in an existing project?
options: Create a Profile model with a OneToOneField
questions.explanation: A profile model with a OneToOneField is the recommended approach for existing projects.

questions.question: To create a group named 'Editors', you would use `Group.objects.______(name='Editors')`.
questions.explanation: `Group.objects.create(name='Editors')` creates the group.

questions.question: Which setting is used to specify a custom user model?
questions.explanation: `AUTH_USER_MODEL = 'myapp.MyUser'` is the setting.

questions.question: The `@permission_required` decorator automatically redirects to the login page if the user is not authenticated.
questions.explanation: True. It uses the same mechanism as `@login_required` for unauthenticated users.

questions.question: What is the default name of the middleware that attaches the user to every request?
questions.explanation: `AuthenticationMiddleware` is included in the default `MIDDLEWARE` list and adds `request.user`.

questions.question: To allow users to log in with email instead of username, you would create a custom ______.
questions.explanation: A custom authentication backend can override the authentication logic.

questions.question: What does `user.groups.add(group)` do?
options: Adds the user to the group
Adds a permission to the group
Removes the user from the group
questions.explanation: It adds the user to the specified group, giving them all permissions of that group.

questions.question: Superusers automatically have all permissions, regardless of group assignments.
questions.explanation: True. `is_superuser` bypasses all permission checks.

questions.question: Which Django signal can be used to automatically create a profile when a user is created?
questions.explanation: `post_save` on the User model is the typical signal for creating related objects.

questions.question: To access the current user in a template, you use the `{{ ______ }}` variable.
questions.explanation: The `user` variable is automatically available in templates when using `RequestContext` (default).
